description: Use when a recording opens fine but has wrong data in it ("fix my run", an odd heart-rate spike, the watch kept running at the start or end). It cleans up what is wrong inside a readable file; it does not fix a file that fails to open or is corrupt. Finds heart-rate spikes (one repair_hr step each; a low-confidence spike is proposed unticked) and an idle stretch at the start or end (one crop step), and reports heart-rate dropouts, which cannot be filled. If the user points at a time ("around minute 20"), pass suspectRanges in elapsed seconds from the start. One activity. Nothing is changed by this call, and nothing that alters heart rate or any other data is applied without the user's confirmation. Show the user every step whose needsUserConfirmation is true, with its title, reason and changes, and get an explicit yes; then call apply_plan with exactly the confirmed step ids. Relay findings and notes in plain words. If refusal is set, tell the user why and do not offer a workaround the answer does not give.

activityId.description: The activity to check, from upload_activity / POST /activities.

sensitivity.description: Spike detector sensitivity, 1 (only obvious spikes) to 5 (anything suspicious). Default 3.

suspectRanges.description: Up to 10 stretches the user thinks are wrong, in elapsed seconds from the activity's first record ("around minute 20" is fromSec 1140, toSec 1260). Each must be 1 to 3600 s long (toSec - fromSec).

fromSec.description: Start of the stretch, seconds from the first record.

toSec.description: End of the stretch, seconds from the first record.

name: analyze_cleanup
